subject: PrismPay: Performance gatekeeper plan and evidence handoff
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@prismpay.com>, Leila Morgan <leila.morgan@prismpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrismPay: Performance gatekeeper plan and evidence handoff

Hi Sam / Leila —

Thanks again for kicking off the onboarding sprint with us. Per our call, attached is a first-pass Performance Gatekeeper Plan (prismpay_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx) and the traffic profile you shared (traffic_profile_prismpay.json) — I pulled both into the bundle for the test team.

High-level acceptance targets we propose for the go/no-go:
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 400ms (stringent cases), and tail (99.9) < 900ms for heavier sequences.
- Throughput: sustain 110 qps steady-state for 30 minutes with <2% error rate.
- Concurrency: support 250 concurrent user sessions (KV cache warmed).
- Tokenization: average response token count expected ~65; please confirm.

Planned test structure (summary):
1) Warm-up: 15m ramp with customer sample prompts to populate KV caches.
2) Baseline run: 20m steady-state at 30 qps to verify single-client performance.
3) Stress run: two 30m windows — 60m total — ramp to target 110 qps with traffic mix (inference vs embeddings) per traffic_profile_prismpay.json.
4) Spike test: short 5m bursts to 220 qps to validate graceful degradation/fallback behavior.

What we need from PrismPay by EOD Wednesday (2026-09-15):
- Finalized representative prompt set (JSONL) and traffic mix.
- Any special instructions for PII or masking during replay.
- Confirmation of the model variant you want pinned for acceptance (suggest: redwood/gpt-medium-v2-q4_8b).

Internal notes / asks for Ben & Monica:
- Ben: please reserve the Dedicated test slot in us-west-2 on 2026-09-22 08:00–12:00 PT; we may need burst capacity the following day.
- Monica: can you validate the replay harness (replay_harness_notes.md) will accept their JSONL and produce the telemetry we specified (latency percentiles, error codes, token counts)?

I'll set up a 30-minute sync for Thursday to walk through the plan and confirm artifacts. If anyone wants a more conservative latency threshold, call it out now.

Thanks,
Irene
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications from our infra side:

- Tokenization: typical response is 50–80 tokens; 65 avg is fine.
- We will provide the JSONL prompt set and traffic mix by EOD Wednesday (we aim for Wednesday morning but will confirm).
- PII: some prompts include phone numbers that should be masked; we'll tag those in the JSONL.

Two asks from us:
1) Can you confirm whether the p99 target is measured at the API gateway or at the model server (we assume end-to-end API)?
2) During the spike test, do you have circuit-breaker thresholds we should expect (timeouts, retries)?

We'll be available for the 30-minute sync on Thursday — Leila and I prefer morning PT.

Best,
Sam
Head of Platform Engineering
PrismPay

Ben / Monica —

Quick internal runbook and who does what:
- Ben: allocate Dedicated pool us-west-2.t3x-large (4 GPU nodes) for the Sept 22 baseline + stress windows. Please include burst policy to allow one additional node for the spike test (pay-as-you-go).
- Monica: ensure the replay harness will emit the following metrics into the shared Drive folder: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99/p999), error code, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant. We need CSV artifact prismpay_test_results_20260913.csv and the raw telemetry JSONs.

Clarifications for Sam: p99 is measured end-to-end at the Redwood API layer — that includes network/ingress and model inference time. Circuit-breaker behavior: our default timeout is 8s; we apply exponential backoff with two retries for 502/504 then fail. We'll surface those retry counts in the test CSV.

I'll slot the Sept 22 test for 08:00–11:30 PT with a 30-minute buffer for post-mortem. Please confirm if PrismPay needs a morning start earlier than 08:00.

Irene

Subject: PrismPay test run results (preliminary) — 2026-09-13 runs

Team / Sam —

We completed the scheduled runs on 2026-09-13 (warm-up + baseline + stress + spike). Summary (preliminary):

- Baseline (30m @ 30 qps): p50=88ms, p95=180ms, p99=350ms, error rate=0.3%
- Stress (2x30m @ ramp to 110 qps): sustained 110 qps for 28/30m in window 1 and 30/30m in window 2. p50=130ms, p95=260ms, p99=510ms, error rate=1.1%
- Spike: brief bursts to 220 qps; graceful degradation observed. Tail p999 peaked ~1.2s; we saw increased retries but no persistent failover to fallback model.

Artifacts uploaded to Drive: prismpay_test_results_20260913.csv (summary CSV), /raw/prismpay/telemetry_20260913/*.json. Also attached are heatmaps and a small batch of flagged responses for quality review.

Action items and notes:
- We hit the throughput threshold but p99 exceeded the proposed 400ms in the stress windows. Recommendation: tune batching window and consider q4_8b quantization profile to reduce inference latency ~8–12%.
- Sam: please review flagged responses for any business-sensitive content and confirm masking is acceptable.
- Next step: if PrismPay is comfortable with the current degradation envelope, we can sign the acceptance document (HubSpot deal link below) and schedule a run with production traffic on a limited rollout. If not, we can run a remediation cycle (estimate 3 business days) to tune the model config and retry.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/PRIS-1234
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG-prismpay-onboard

Thanks — I can walk through the CSV in tomorrow's 30-minute review.

—Monica
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
